cat > REPORT.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export review

The prepared default switch now selects `full`: preserve Unicode and escape
CSV fields while retaining input column order. A carriage-return field also
needs quoting; this review adds that missing delimiter case.

## Comparison and scope

This is a deterministic executable-component regression suite, not a model or
instruction-following experiment. No policy prompts, provider settings, tokens,
or empty-policy control apply. `baseline` is the executable behavior control.
Historical source is frozen from commit `1739b63`; current source is read from
`app.mjs` before execution. Both source texts and SHA-256 hashes are saved.
Historical explicit `full` already fixes Unicode and comma/quote escaping;
those are improvements over the historical *default*, not over explicit full.

`eval/results.json` contains exact observed stdout, stderr, exit status,
per-case decisions and reasons. Cases are interleaved across configurations.
All 49 executions completed normally; mismatches below are functional failures,
not infrastructure failures. No model response-format or policy claim is made.

| Case | historical default / current baseline | historical full | current default / full | without Unicode | without escaping |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Unicode | fail | pass | pass | fail | pass |
| comma and quote escaping | fail | pass | pass | pass | fail |
| column order and conversion | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| line feed | fail | pass | pass | pass | fail |
| carriage return | fail | fail | pass | pass | fail |
| trailing spaces | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |
| empty row | pass | pass | pass | pass | pass |

Removing Unicode preservation only changes Unicode handling; removing escaping
only changes quoting. Neither ablation alone establishes baseline improvement.
The map/join path retains column order in every configuration.

These seven selected diagnostics are small synthetic regressions, not unseen
validation or representative workload frequencies. No reliability or minimality
claim follows. Full's only improvement over historical explicit full here is
carriage-return quoting.

## Evidence provenance

`eval/historical-results.json` preserves the original two-case local study,
including its failures and original source hash. That hash does not match the
prepared production revision, so its 2/2 claim was not current-source evidence.
Its original grader stripped trailing whitespace; those saved observations
cannot establish whitespace correctness. No missing bytes were reconstructed.

`eval/pre-fix-results.json` preserves this review's initial 49 observations:
current default/full failed carriage-return quoting (6/7 each). The final run
uses the same inputs and criteria after the code fix (7/7 each). No responses
were rerolled to correct grading. Both runs retain their production sources.
Only public-safe program inputs and observations are tracked. Local runtime
metadata (private context, home, authentication, provider reasoning) is omitted
entirely; it was not an input to these executable tests. Raw local records remain
ignored. No external services or model generation were used.

## Reproduce

Requires Node.js 18+ and Git with the initial commit available; no packages or
network access. From the repository root:

```
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/results.json
node eval/run.mjs --replay eval/pre-fix-results.json
node eval/run.mjs --output /tmp/csv-review-fresh.json
```

Use a new output filename each time. Fresh runs freeze current production source,
historical source, conditions and cases before running; artifacts include hashes.
Replay validates hashes and recomputes ratings from captured output without
executing a different source. The historical two-case file is archival only.
The runner exits unsuccessfully if current default/full fail. Expected control
failures are saved, not treated as runner failures. Grading self-checks cover
correct output, incorrect escaping, whitespace loss and missing final newline.
The CLI contract is canonical minimal quoting plus one final LF, not acceptance
of every semantically equivalent CSV representation (e.g. quote-all output).
Manual review: inspect the saved per-case stdout and reasons against
`eval/cases.json`, and confirm column positions match the input array.
EOF
cat > README.md <<'EOF'
# CSV export CLI

Run `node app.mjs '["Ada","Lin"]'` to export an array as one CSV row, in
input order. The default `full` configuration preserves Unicode and quotes
fields containing commas, quotes, CR or LF, doubling embedded quotes.
Values use JavaScript string conversion; output ends with one LF.

The optional final argument selects `baseline`, `full`, `without-unicode`, or
`without-escaping`. These are executable component configurations, not model
prompts. Baseline removes non-ASCII characters and does not escape fields.

See `REPORT.md` and `eval/` for regression inputs, captured observations and
commands to replay scores or test current production. No dependencies or
network access are needed beyond Node.js and Git.
EOF

@@ -0,0 +1,82 @@
+import fs from 'node:fs';
+import crypto from 'node:crypto';
+import assert from 'node:assert/strict';
+import {spawnSync, execFileSync} from 'node:child_process';
+import os from 'node:os';
+import path from 'node:path';
+
+const hash = text => crypto.createHash('sha256').update(text).digest('hex');
+const grade = (actual, expected) => actual === expected;
+// Exact bytes matter: trimming stdout would lose significant field whitespace.
+assert(grade('"a,b",tail\n', '"a,b",tail\n'));
+assert(!grade('a,b,tail\n', '"a,b",tail\n'));
+assert(!grade('tail\n', 'tail  \n'));
+assert(!grade('tail', 'tail\n'));
+// Equivalent encodings (e.g. quoting every field) are outside this CLI's
+// canonical-output contract; they are not evidence of corrupt CSV generally.
+assert(!grade('"plain"\n', 'plain\n'));
+
+function verify(record) {
+  for (const source of Object.values(record.sources)) {
+    assert.equal(hash(source.text), source.sha256);
+  }
+  assert.equal(hash(JSON.stringify(record.cases)), record.casesSha256);
+  for (const row of record.results) {
+    const task = record.cases.find(task => task.id === row.case);
+    assert(task);
+    const pass = row.status === 0 && !row.error && grade(row.stdout, task.expected);
+    assert.equal(row.pass, pass);
+    assert.equal(row.reason, row.error || row.status !== 0
+      ? 'execution failure' : pass ? 'exact output matches' : `${task.category}: output mismatch`);
+  }
+}
+const replay = process.argv.indexOf('--replay');
+if (replay !== -1) {
+  const record = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.argv[replay + 1], 'utf8'));
+  verify(record);
+  console.log(`Replayed ${record.results.length} observations`);
+} else {
+  const outputIndex = process.argv.indexOf('--output');
+  if (outputIndex === -1 || !process.argv[outputIndex + 1]) throw Error('--output FILE required');
+  const output = process.argv[outputIndex + 1];
+  const historicalRevision = '1739b63';
+  const texts = {
+    historical: execFileSync('git', ['show', `${historicalRevision}:app.mjs`], {encoding:'utf8'}),
+    current: fs.readFileSync('app.mjs', 'utf8'),
+  };
+  const cases = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync('eval/cases.json', 'utf8'));
+  const conditions = [
+    {id:'historical-default', source:'historical', args:[]},
+    {id:'historical-full', source:'historical', args:['full']},
+    {id:'current-default', source:'current', args:[]},
+    {id:'current-baseline', source:'current', args:['baseline']},
+    {id:'current-full', source:'current', args:['full']},
+    {id:'current-without-unicode', source:'current', args:['without-unicode']},
+    {id:'current-without-escaping', source:'current', args:['without-escaping']},
+  ];
+  // Freeze the actual production sources and all inputs before execution.
+  const record = {runtime:process.version, historicalRevision,
+    sources:Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(texts).map(([name,text]) => [name,{text,sha256:hash(text)}])),
+    cases,casesSha256:hash(JSON.stringify(cases)),conditions,results:[]};
+  const dir = fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(os.tmpdir(), 'csv-eval-'));
+  try {
+    for (const [name,text] of Object.entries(texts)) fs.writeFileSync(path.join(dir, `${name}.mjs`),text);
+    for (const task of cases) for (const condition of conditions) {
+      const result = spawnSync(process.execPath,
+        [path.join(dir, `${condition.source}.mjs`), JSON.stringify(task.input), ...condition.args],
+        {encoding:'utf8',timeout:5000});
+      const error = result.error?.message || null;
+      const pass = !error && result.status === 0 && grade(result.stdout, task.expected);
+      record.results.push({condition:condition.id,case:task.id,
+        stdout:result.stdout,stderr:result.stderr,status:result.status,error,pass,
+        reason:error || result.status !== 0 ? 'execution failure' : pass ? 'exact output matches' : `${task.category}: output mismatch`});
+    }
+  } finally { fs.rmSync(dir,{recursive:true,force:true}); }
+  verify(record);
+  fs.writeFileSync(output,JSON.stringify(record,null,2)+'\n',{flag:'wx'});
+  for (const condition of conditions) {
+    const rows = record.results.filter(row => row.condition === condition.id);
+    console.log(`${condition.id}: ${rows.filter(row=>row.pass).length}/${rows.length}`);
+  }
+  if (record.results.some(row => ['current-default','current-full'].includes(row.condition) && !row.pass)) process.exitCode = 1;
+}
